standard_prerequisites.use: The Picard setup and characterization of Z (lemma-diagonal-picard-flat-proper, same chapter), the scheme-theoretic image reach-points criterion (Morphisms), and the triviality of invertible sheaves over valuation rings at the generic point (same chapter); cited inputs with the valuative argument written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Reduce closedness of Z to the valuative criterion via finite presentation of j : Z -> S and the reach-points lemma.
For a valuation ring map g : Spec(A) -> S with generic point in Z, use the triviality-over-valuation-ring lemma.
Conclude via the characterization of Z in the setup lemma that the closed point also lies in Z, hence Z is closed.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce closedness to the valuative criterion for valuation rings.
Verify the valuative condition from triviality over valuation rings and the characterization of Z.

difficulty_reason: In the Picard setup of the diagonal lemma (f flat proper with a relatively generated invertible sheaf E, Z the locus where the fibre of E is trivial), adding that E is invertible and the geometric fibres are integral makes Z closed in S. The proof is a written valuative reduction: since Z -> S is of finite presentation, closedness follows from the reach-points lemma applied to valuation rings, and the valuative condition itself follows from the triviality-over-valuation-ring lemma together with the characterization of Z in the setup lemma. Retained author proof at lines 9418-9427.
